name: Viloxazine ER (Qelbree)
summary: Once-daily, non-stimulant ADHD medication that works on norepinephrine. Not a controlled substance, but it carries a serious warning about suicidal thoughts—especially early on or with dose changes.
description: Qelbree (viloxazine ER) is a non-stimulant medication for ADHD in kids (6+) and adults. It’s taken once daily and can help with focus, follow-through, and impulsivity over time—not usually within hours. The biggest safety headline is suicidal thoughts/behaviors: people need close monitoring for mood or behavior changes, especially in the first few months and whenever the dose changes. It can also raise heart rate and blood pressure, and it can make some people sleepy while making others more wired or insomniac.
patient_summary: Qelbree is a once-daily, non-stimulant ADHD med. It’s not typically an “instant fix”—most people notice benefits over weeks. The big safety issue is suicidal thoughts/behaviors, so you (and anyone close to you) should watch for mood changes, irritability, agitation, or dark thoughts—especially early on and when the dose changes. It can also raise heart rate and blood pressure, and it may cause sleepiness or insomnia.

linked_conditions.context: FDA-labeled for ADHD in adults and in children ages 6 and older. Often considered when someone wants a non-stimulant option, can’t tolerate stimulants, or has concern about stimulant misuse.

contraindications: Concomitant use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI
Concomitant use of sensitive CYP1A2 substrates or CYP1A2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic range

efficacy_response.patient_text: In clinical trials, Qelbree improved core ADHD symptoms (inattention, impulsivity, hyperactivity) compared with placebo. It’s typically not an immediate “same-day” switch—most people notice meaningful change over weeks, with dose adjustments based on benefit and side effects.

pharmacokinetics.absorption: May be decreased with a high-fat meal; high-fat meals may delay time to peak concentration by about 2 hours
pharmacokinetics.onset: Not a rapid-onset medication; benefits usually build over days to weeks
pharmacokinetics.food_effect: High-fat meal may delay Tmax by ~2 hours; absorption may be reduced with high-fat intake

sections.heading: What It's Used For
sections.text: Qelbree (viloxazine ER) is a non-stimulant medication used to treat {link:condition:attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder:ADHD}. The goal is better attention, follow-through, organization, and less impulsivity. It’s taken once daily, and improvements often build over time rather than hitting all at once.
items: {link:condition:attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder:ADHD}: Difficulty sustaining attention, forgetfulness, disorganization, impulsive decisions, restlessness, and follow-through problems

sections.heading: What People Feel
sections.intro: Real talk: this one can feel different depending on your baseline (already tired vs already wired) and where your dose lands. Here’s what people commonly report:

quotes: I didn’t feel a “kick.” I just realized I was finishing stuff again.
My brain felt less scattered. Less tab-switching.
It wasn’t dramatic—more like the day got easier to steer.
It made me sleepy at first—like a heavy eyelid vibe.
I got insomnia the first couple of weeks and had to change my routine.
Once I adjusted, my sleep evened out, but the start was weird.
items.note: Drowsiness and insomnia both show up in real life. If sleep flips the wrong way, dose timing and pace of titration matter.

quotes: My stomach was not impressed the first week.
I had headaches for a bit, then they faded.
My appetite dipped and I had to remind myself to eat.

items.category: Mood Watch (this is the big one)
quotes: I got more irritable and snappy, and it freaked me out.
I felt down in a way that didn’t match my life—like a cloud rolled in.
If dark thoughts show up, I’m not “pushing through.” I’m calling my doctor.
items.note: This medication has a warning for suicidal thoughts/behaviors. You’re not being dramatic by taking mood changes seriously—early reporting is the whole point.

sections.heading: How Fast It Works
sections.text: Qelbree is not usually a same-day “I feel it in an hour” medication. It’s once daily, and benefits typically build over time as your dose is adjusted to the sweet spot.
key_points: First doses: Side effects (like nausea, sleepiness, or insomnia) can show up before benefits
Days to weeks: Gradual improvement in attention, follow-through, and impulsivity is more typical than an instant shift
~5 hours: Average time to peak level after a dose (food—especially high-fat—can delay this)
~7 hours: Reported half-life (extended-release formulation supports once-daily use)

sections.heading: How Well It Works
sections.text: In clinical trials, Qelbree improved ADHD symptoms compared with placebo. The effect is usually more “my day runs smoother” than “my brain changed in 30 minutes.” Dose adjustments are typically weekly, and the goal is steady benefit without mood or cardiovascular side effects.
sections.clinical_details: Viloxazine ER is a non-stimulant option for ADHD with once-daily dosing. Response is assessed by functional outcomes (task completion, sustained attention, impulsivity, organization) and tolerability (sleep, appetite, mood, blood pressure/heart rate). Because the medication has a suicidality warning, symptom improvement isn’t the only target—mood stability and safety monitoring are part of the treatment plan from day one.

sections.heading: Critical Safety Information
sections.highlight: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors have been reported more often with viloxazine than placebo in ADHD trials. Monitor closely—especially early on and with dose changes.
sections.black_box: In clinical studies, higher rates of suicidal thoughts and behavior were reported in patients with ADHD treated with viloxazine than with placebo. Closely monitor all viloxazine-treated patients for clinical worsening, and for emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
other: Mood and behavior changes can be warning signs: new or worsening depression, irritability, agitation, insomnia, impulsivity, aggression/hostility, panic symptoms, or unusual behavior changes
Cardiovascular effects: can increase heart rate and diastolic blood pressure; tachycardia has been reported
Sedation/fatigue can impair driving and tasks that require alertness
Mania/hypomania risk: use caution in bipolar disorder; screen for bipolar history and family history before starting
Pregnancy risk: animal data suggest fetal harm; consider discontinuing if pregnancy occurs during treatment (per manufacturer guidance)
MAOI interaction is a hard stop: do not use with MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI
patient_counseling: If suicidal thoughts show up, or your mood shifts in a scary way, contact your clinician right away. If you feel unsafe, go to emergency services.
Have a family member/partner/friend keep an eye on mood and behavior changes early in treatment and during dose changes—outside observers often catch patterns first.
Check blood pressure and pulse as directed. Report chest pain, fainting, unexplained shortness of breath, or severe palpitations.
Don’t drive or operate machinery until you know how sleepy (or wired) this makes you.
Tell your prescriber if you’ve ever had bipolar symptoms, manic episodes, or a strong family history of bipolar disorder or suicide.

sections.heading: Side Effects
sections.summary: The most common side effects involve sleep/energy (drowsiness, fatigue, insomnia), GI upset (nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting), headache, appetite decrease, and irritability. It can also raise heart rate and diastolic blood pressure. Suicidal ideation is uncommon but serious—and it’s why monitoring matters.
plain_language_list: Nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, constipation, reflux
Decreased appetite and possible weight loss (reported in adolescents)
Increased heart rate and increased diastolic blood pressure

common.patient_note: Some people notice a faster pulse, palpitations, or feeling “keyed up.” This is a monitor-it side effect—especially if you have cardiac history or symptoms.
This is why baseline and follow-up BP checks are not optional. If readings climb or you feel symptoms (headache, chest discomfort, dizziness), tell your clinician.
You might feel slowed down, heavy, or foggy—especially early on. Don’t gamble with driving until you know your response.
Often shows up early. If it’s severe, persistent, or paired with concerning BP changes, it needs attention.
Some people get more awake or restless. Sleep changes can be a side effect—and can also be an early warning sign for mood activation. Report it if it’s new or escalating.
GI side effects are common early. Food timing may help, but don’t crush or chew the capsule.
Not everyone gets appetite suppression, but if you do, it can sneak up. Track meals and weight, especially in adolescents.
If irritability feels like a personality change, or it escalates quickly, don’t brush it off—especially early in treatment.

serious: Suicidal thoughts or behaviors: needs urgent clinical contact and close monitoring, especially in the first months and during dose changes
Mania/hypomania or mixed symptoms: decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, risky behavior, extreme irritability—stop-and-call-your-clinician territory
Clinically significant cardiovascular symptoms: exertional chest pain, fainting, severe palpitations, or other signs of heart disease need prompt evaluation
Severe allergic reaction (rare): swelling, rash with breathing difficulty—emergency care

sections.heading: Critical Drug Interactions
sections.intro: The big interaction themes with Qelbree are: MAOIs (contraindicated) and CYP enzyme effects—especially strong CYP1A2 inhibition, which can dangerously raise levels of certain medications.

items.risk: Contraindicated. Serious interaction risk if used together or too close together.
items.action: Do not use Qelbree with an MAOI or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI.

items.with: Sensitive CYP1A2 substrates (or CYP1A2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic range)
items.risk: Qelbree strongly inhibits CYP1A2, which can raise levels of certain medications to unsafe ranges.
items.action: Avoid these combinations or use an alternative ADHD medication. If a combination is being considered, the prescriber needs a plan—not vibes.

items.with: Other medications that raise heart rate or blood pressure
items.action: Monitor BP and pulse closely, especially during titration and dose increases.

items.risk: Can worsen drowsiness/fatigue and impair alertness.
items.action: Use caution and avoid risky activities until you know your level of sedation.

sections.heading: Safe Discontinuation
sections.text: Qelbree is not a benzodiazepine and is not typically associated with dangerous withdrawal the way sedatives are. That said, don’t stop abruptly just to “see what happens.” If you stop suddenly, you can get rebound ADHD symptoms (worse focus/impulsivity), mood swings, or sleep disruption. If discontinuation is needed, a clinician may recommend a gradual step-down based on your dose, side effects, and how you’re functioning.
key_points: Stopping suddenly may bring back ADHD symptoms quickly (and sometimes harder than expected)
If mood symptoms emerged on treatment, your clinician may want a careful plan to stop and monitor
If you’re on a higher dose, a gradual reduction can reduce rebound insomnia, irritability, and functional whiplash
If you ever stop because of suicidal thoughts, severe mood change, mania symptoms, or cardiac symptoms: safety comes first—contact your clinician immediately

sections.heading: Dosing Information
sections.text: Qelbree is taken once daily. Adult titration is usually weekly, with dose increases based on response and side effects. Capsules must be swallowed whole or opened and sprinkled (no chewing).

adult.adhd_titration: Increase by 200 mg increments at weekly intervals based on response and tolerability
adult.renal_severe_initial: 100 mg PO once daily (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2)
adult.renal_severe_titration: Increase by 50 to 100 mg increments at weekly intervals based on response and tolerability

sections.simple_explanation: This is a once-daily, extended-release capsule. You don’t crush or chew it. If swallowing capsules is hard, you can open it and sprinkle the full contents on a spoonful of applesauce or pudding, swallow without chewing, and use it right away (don’t store it for later).

sections.heading: Pregnancy, Breastfeeding, Special Groups
sections.text: Special population guidance with Qelbree is mostly about pregnancy/lactation risk, pediatric monitoring, and kidney impairment dosing. Mood monitoring matters across all ages.
sections.pregnancy: Animal reproduction studies suggest in utero exposure may cause fetal harm. For mild to moderate ADHD in pregnancy, nonpharmacologic approaches are generally preferred. If pregnancy occurs during treatment, the manufacturer recommends considering discontinuation, using shared decision-making that weighs the risks of untreated ADHD versus medication exposure. Patients can be enrolled in the National Pregnancy Registry for Psychiatric Medications (1-866-961-2388).
sections.lactation: Viloxazine and its metabolite are present in breast milk. In a small dataset (15 lactating women taking 600 mg daily for 3 days), estimated relative infant doses were low (around 1% for viloxazine and 0.7% for the metabolite). The decision to breastfeed during therapy should weigh infant exposure risk, breastfeeding benefits, and the benefits of treating the parent. Monitor infants for feeding difficulties, irritability, and insomnia.
sections.pediatrics: Labeled for ADHD in ages 6 and older. Because it can raise heart rate and blood pressure and has a suicidality warning, pediatric patients need baseline cardiovascular assessment (history, family history, meds list, focused exam) and close behavioral monitoring—especially in the first months and during dose changes. Family members/caregivers should watch daily for mood or behavior changes.
sections.hepatic: No specific dose adjustments are provided in manufacturer labeling for mild to severe hepatic impairment. Use clinical judgment and monitor tolerability, especially sedation and mood changes.
sections.renal: Mild to moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30 to 89 mL/min/1.73 m2): no dose adjustment. Severe impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2): lower starting dose and lower max dose (see adult dosing section).

sections.heading: Clinical Monitoring
items: Suicidal thoughts/behavior monitoring: clinical worsening, new or worsening depression, irritability, agitation, insomnia, anxiety/panic symptoms, impulsivity, aggression/hostility, akathisia, psychosis, hypomania, or mania—especially during the first few months and at times of dose changes
Baseline screening for personal/family history of suicide, bipolar disorder, and depression before starting
Blood pressure and pulse: baseline, after dose increases, and periodically during treatment

Cardiac risk assessment before treatment: patient history, family history of sudden death/ventricular arrhythmia, medication review, and focused cardiovascular exam; additional evaluation (ECG/echo) if findings suggest risk
Prompt cardiac evaluation during treatment if exertional chest pain, unexplained syncope, or other cardiac symptoms develop
Sedation and functional safety: assess daytime sleepiness, driving safety, and performance at school/work
Sleep tracking: insomnia vs hypersomnia, plus sleep changes as a potential mood-activation signal
Weight and appetite (especially in adolescents): watch for decreased appetite and weight loss
Kidney function: serum creatinine and GFR, especially if impairment is present or suspected
Liver enzymes: monitor as clinically indicated and if symptoms suggest hepatic issues
Periodic reassessment of long-term usefulness: is it improving functioning enough to justify continued use at the current dose?

sections.heading: Available Formulations
sections.text: Qelbree is an extended-release capsule taken once daily. The capsule must not be crushed, chewed, or cut. If needed, it can be opened and sprinkled on a small amount of applesauce or pudding and swallowed without chewing.
items: Extended-release capsules (24 hour): 100 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg

sections.heading: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: Qelbree works mainly by blocking the reuptake of norepinephrine (it keeps more norepinephrine available in key brain circuits). That’s one of the core neurotransmitters involved in attention, alertness, and impulse control. The full ADHD mechanism isn’t completely mapped out, but there’s also evidence from lab data that it affects serotonin receptors (including 5-HT2B and 5-HT2C), which may help explain why it can impact sleep, appetite, and mood in some people.

sections.heading: Place in Treatment Algorithm
sections.text: Qelbree is a non-stimulant ADHD option that fits best when someone wants once-daily coverage and would rather avoid a controlled substance, or when stimulants aren’t tolerated (side effects, anxiety, sleep disruption, appetite issues) or aren’t appropriate. The tradeoff is that it usually builds benefit over time and requires real monitoring—especially for mood changes and suicidal thoughts early in treatment and around dose changes. It can also push heart rate and blood pressure up, so cardiovascular check-ins are part of the deal.

seo.title: Viloxazine ER (Qelbree): Uses, Dosing, Side Effects & Suicidality Warning
seo.description: Qelbree (viloxazine ER) is a once-daily, non-stimulant ADHD medication. Learn dosing (200–600 mg), kidney adjustments, common side effects (sleep changes, nausea, headache), blood pressure/heart rate monitoring, and the suicidal thoughts warning.

editorial.reviewStatement: Content medically reviewed and verified against FDA prescribing information, APA clinical practice guidelines, and current peer-reviewed literature.

faqs.a: Qelbree (viloxazine ER) is used to treat ADHD in adults and in kids ages 6 and up. It’s a non-stimulant option meant to improve attention, follow-through, organization, and impulsivity over time.

Most people don’t feel an immediate “kick.” Side effects can show up early, but benefits usually build over days to weeks. The dose is typically adjusted weekly to find the best balance of improvement and tolerability.
No. Qelbree is not a controlled substance. It’s a non-stimulant ADHD medication.

faqs.q: What’s the most important warning with Qelbree?
faqs.a: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors have been reported more often with viloxazine than placebo in ADHD studies. People should be closely monitored for mood or behavior changes—especially in the first few months of treatment and anytime the dose changes.

faqs.q: What mood or behavior changes should I watch for?
faqs.a: Call your prescriber right away for new or worsening depression, irritability, agitation, insomnia, anxiety/panic symptoms, impulsivity, aggression/hostility, akathisia, psychosis, or hypomania/mania. If you feel unsafe or at immediate risk, seek emergency help.

faqs.q: Can Qelbree affect heart rate or blood pressure?
faqs.a: Yes. Qelbree commonly increases heart rate and diastolic blood pressure. This is why clinicians monitor blood pressure and pulse at baseline, after dose increases, and periodically during treatment. Report chest pain, fainting, or severe palpitations immediately.

faqs.q: What are the most common Qelbree side effects?
faqs.a: Common side effects include sleepiness/sedation or fatigue, insomnia (especially in adults), headache, nausea and other GI symptoms, decreased appetite, and irritability. Heart rate and blood pressure increases are also common.

faqs.q: How do you take Qelbree if you can’t swallow capsules?
faqs.a: You can swallow the capsule whole, or open it and sprinkle the entire contents onto a teaspoon of applesauce or pudding. Swallow without chewing. Use the mixture right away (within 15 minutes for pudding or within 2 hours for applesauce) and don’t store it for later.

faqs.q: What’s the usual adult dose for ADHD?
faqs.a: Adults typically start at 200 mg once daily. The dose can be increased by 200 mg each week based on response and side effects, up to a maximum of 600 mg per day. In severe kidney impairment, dosing starts lower and the maximum dose is lower.

People taking MAOIs (or who stopped an MAOI within the last 14 days) should not take Qelbree. It’s also contraindicated with certain sensitive CYP1A2 medications (especially those with a narrow therapeutic range). Your prescriber should review your full medication list before starting.

faqs.q: Is Qelbree safe in pregnancy or breastfeeding?
faqs.a: Animal data suggest fetal harm risk, and the manufacturer recommends considering discontinuation if pregnancy occurs during treatment. Viloxazine and a metabolite are present in breast milk, and decisions about breastfeeding should weigh infant exposure risk against the benefits of breastfeeding and treatment. Shared decision-making is key, and pregnancy registry enrollment is encouraged.

It can potentially trigger mania/hypomania or a mixed episode in people with bipolar disorder. Clinicians should screen for bipolar disorder and risk factors before starting, and any signs of mood activation (decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, risky behavior, extreme irritability) should be reported immediately.
